is_anopheles.evidence: Mosquitoes collected by human landing catches were identified as Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus (Page 3, Entomological measurements; Page 5, Entomological indexes).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The authors genotyped the L1014F kdr allele using the Martinez-Torres method (Page 3, Laboratory examination) and reported its frequency in M and S molecular forms of An. gambiae s.s. (Page 5, Entomological indexes).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 5 reports that a total of 115 An. gambiae s.l. mosquitoes were collected and analyzed, with L1014F kdr allele frequencies of 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37-0.57) in the M form and 0.61 (95% CI: 0.43-0.80) in the S form.

african_field_population.evidence: Adult mosquitoes were collected using human landing catches between December 2007 and November 2008 in seven villages in the Ouidah-Kpomassè-Tori Bossito health district, southern Benin (Page 2, Site description & Sampling; Page 3, Entomological measurements).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical epidemiological and entomological field study conducted in southern Benin.

sub_country_location.evidence: Table 1 (Page 3) lists 7 specific villages (Aïdjèdo, Dokanmè, Kindjitokpa, Guézohoué, Hèkandji, Satré, Wanho) along with their spatial coordinates in the Ouidah-Kpomassè-Tori Bossito health district.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito collection and clinical monitoring took place from December 2007 to November 2008 (Page 2, Site description).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper describes a standard primary field study carried out in southern Benin without indication of dataset duplication.

supplement.evidence: All primary entomological and kdr genotype frequency data mentioned in the study are reported directly within the main text.

assessment.summary: This longitudinal epidemiological and entomological study evaluated malaria infection, disease, and vector control in seven villages of the Ouidah-Kpomassè-Tori Bossito health district in southern Benin from December 2007 to November 2008. Field-caught Anopheles gambiae s.l. (115 specimens) were molecularly identified to M and S forms and genotyped for the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) mutation, yielding allele frequencies of 0.47 in the M form and 0.61 in the S form.
